chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, from one of the Imams of the Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) took the women with him in the war, and they treated the wounded. He did not allocate for them any share of the spoils (al-fay'), but rather granted them a voluntary bonus (nafa'l).

key_terms.الْفَيْءُ: Spoils of war or booty, specifically the portion acquired without battle.
key_terms.نَفَّلَهُنَّ: He granted them a voluntary bonus or extra gift, distinct from the fixed share.
key_terms.يُدَاوِينَ الْجَرْحَى: They treated the wounded, indicating the specific role of women in this context.

ai.seo_question: Did women receive a share of the spoils of war when they accompanied the Prophet in battle?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between the fixed quarter-share of spoils (*fay'*) reserved for combatants and the discretionary stipend (*nafa'l*) granted to women who served in a non-combatant medical capacity. It establishes the precedent for compensating auxiliary participants in warfare, a principle widely cited by Shia jurists when discussing the distribution of war booty and the status of women in early Islamic military expeditions.
